key_observations_html:
• U.S. ETP 30d net flow rose 93.4% vs prior 30D: Listed-product flows printing +$7.29B (93.4% vs prior 30D) indicate investors are still using ETPs as the primary regulated gateway into crypto beta—supporting demand even when spot prices are choppy. Related: Strive acquires 1,110 bitcoin for $81.5 million as total holdings reach 21,356 BTC (The Block).
  • Forward market-size scenarios are large, but still assumptions-driven: Public analyst commentary continues to frame the next few years in a broad range—for example, one widely cited 2026 scenario set points to roughly $180B–$220B for Bitcoin ETF assets, compared with about $90.56B across U.S. spot Bitcoin ETPs on this page today (see ). Treat these as directional planning ranges, not a base-case forecast. Related: Zcash hits eight-year high near $850 with futures volume near $10 billion amid Grayscale ETF push (The Block).
  • The filing pipeline remains crowded: Most filings will not scale, but active pipelines still foreshadow which issuers and custodians will compete hardest for the next wave of listings. Related: Grayscale moves closer to launching first Zcash ETF in US with fresh amended SEC filing (The Block).
  • Product access expanded quickly, then concentrated: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETP approvals in 2024 (see ) widened listed access fast—yet the top three funds still carry about 67% of listed AUM here (IBIT ($58.78B), FBTC ($13.43B), GBTC ($10.13B)). For allocators and service providers, scale and distribution economics now matter at least as much as first-mover timing. Related: Crypto roars back as bitcoin posts its second-best week since early 2021 (CoinDesk).
